doc.title: Mike Davis interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, April 1, 2024

title: Charts with no improvisation
summary: Davis discusses his 2019 brass quintet record with no improvising and Rowe's short charts needing a solo.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: Have you written a chart that has no improvised sections in it? No solo sax, nothing?

Yeah quite a few actually, but almost all of them are for brass that I’ve done for that. I did a brass quintet record in 2019 and there’s no improvising on that record at all. It’s just a standard brass quintet: two trumpets, French horn, trombone and tuba. And all the players could improvise and had the versatility to play whatever stylistically was put in front of them. And you know it’s classically oriented but it has that accessibility factor that I’m always trying to go for. But it’s certainly not jazz even in an improvised way or harmonically. There are jazz elements but there’s no improvisation.
The few times I’ve tried that, I’ll work and work and work and then I’ll play it back and I go I like it except it’s only like 70 seconds long. It’s time for a solo.
Yeah. There’s something nice about being able to rely on improvisation to beef up a chart a little bit.
